messages:
lia: New standing desk arrived! finally swapped the cheap one for something my back will thank me for. also my ficus keeps photobombing Zoom and my home Wi-Fi started jittering after I moved things around. pic: https://files.redwood.com/lia/desk_ficus.jpg
aj: Oooo love the lamp + plant :plant: looks very cozy
maria: congrats on the desk! router logs or a ping trace? could be interference from the desk hardware or a new placement blocking signal
lia: it started acting up right after I shifted the desk against that bookshelf. trying a quick ping now — looked noisy
```
PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=117 time=28.3 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=117 time=120.6 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=3 ttl=117 time=27.9 ms
--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
4 packets transmitted, 3 packets received, 25% packet loss
```
devon: that packet loss screams interference. first moves: lift router up, avoid behind big metal bookends, and try 5GHz if your laptop supports it
aj: and if you have a mesh kit, make sure the primary node is not behind anything dense. also try changing 5GHz channel to one less busy
sam: if you want a quick restart:
```
sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager  # on linux laptop
# or from your router's admin UI -> System -> Reboot
ssh root@192.168.0.1 'reboot'  # if you're comfy with ssh to router
```
lia: i'll try moving the router to the top shelf and do a reboot. also — any cable management ideas for under the standing desk? it's spaghetti central rn
maria: zip ties + adhesive cable clips. ikea makes a cable sleeve that hides everything. and label the chargers :)
aj: velcro straps are life. also put a small tray for the power strip so it doesn't hang when you raise/lower the desk
ops-bot: FYI: building ops scheduled a brief power check 2026-03-24 02:00 UTC — might briefly affect home routers if your UPSs are empty (reaction: :alarm_clock:)
lia: thanks for the heads up ops-bot :eyes: i'll do the move + reboot now
(devon: workaround) if you keep seeing drops you can try disabling legacy 802.11b/g on 2.4GHz to cut noise
aj: pro tip: coaster under the ficus pot to avoid water stains on the desk :droplet:
lia: moved the router to the top shelf and restarted — ping looks much better now, no packet loss. wifi feels snappier. pic: https://files.redwood.com/lia/desk_after.jpg (reaction: :partyparrot:)
devon: nice! ergonomic win + wifi win. congrats on adulting successfully :tada:
aj: show us cable pics later pls, i live for good cable management photos :camera_with_flash:
maria: solid work team. also voted "show cable pics" in the imaginary poll (jk)
lia: maybe later tonight. for now i'm celebrating with coffee :coffee: — thanks everyone for the tips!"
